threads.body: [Javaagent] Vert.x 4.4.5 joins batch failures with `System.lineSeparator()`, which is LF on Unix. Two prefix-only failures produce `ERR [0] PrefixOnly\nERR [1] PrefixOnly`; this parser then returns `PrefixOnly\nERR`, corrupting `error.type` on spans and duration metrics. Recognize LF as well as CRLF before extracting the first batch error, and cover a batch containing multiple prefix-only replies.

replies.body: Batch completion now carries the original decoder-confirmed error and its request index into the aggregate. It no longer parses the joined message, so LF or CRLF separators cannot become part of the prefix. The batch regression with multiple prefix-only replies checks the resulting classification on both spans and duration metrics.

threads.body: [Javaagent] `ErrorType` alone does not establish server origin. Vert.x 4.4.5's `RESPParser` also uses it for local decoding failures such as `ILLEGAL_STATE ...` and `Invalid boolean value ...`. Its `batch()` wraps transport failures in this class too, so a wrapped `CONNECTION_CLOSED` bypasses the exact-message exclusion below. These paths emit message tokens as server codes instead of exception-class fallback. Preserve whether an error came from a decoded server error reply, and return null for locally generated failures; cover decoding and batch connection failures.

replies.body: Addressed by capturing server-error provenance at `RESPParser.handleError`, rather than trusting `ErrorType` or its message. Local decoder failures and wrapped batch transport failures retain exception-class fallback. The `localDecoderFailure` and `wrappedBatchTransportFailure` integration cases cover both spans and duration metrics.

threads.body: [Javaagent] Matching this message shape does not establish that Vert.x added a batch wrapper. A single-command `redis.error_reply('ERR [0] application detail')` is classified as `application` instead of `ERR`, putting message text into span and duration-metric `error.type`. Also, Vert.x 4.4.5's `batch()` strips the original leading `ERR ` before wrapping, so a server reply `ERR wrong number of arguments ...` becomes `wrong`. Preserve the decoded prefix before this lossy rewrite and distinguish confirmed batch wrappers from raw replies. Add regression coverage for both cases.

replies.body: The prefix is now captured from the original decoded reply before Vert.x strips `ERR` or adds batch indexes. Wrapper-looking text is not used to infer provenance. Regression cases cover the single-command reply `ERR [0] application detail` and batched `ERR wrong number of arguments`; both retain `ERR` on spans and duration metrics.

threads.body: [Javaagent] With a sufficiently high `maxNestedArrays` setting, Vert.x can decode a deeply nested array successfully, but the recursive `getResponseError()` traversal can throw `StackOverflowError`. Vert.x 4.4.5 parses and unwinds these arrays iteratively. Here, the error fails only the discarded `whenComplete` stage: execution never reaches `result.complete(value)`, so the application's otherwise successful `send()` or `batch()` future remains pending indefinitely. Use an iterative or bounded best-effort traversal, and isolate and log inspection failures so the original application outcome is still forwarded. Add a regression using a deeply nested successful reply.

Inspection and span-ending failures are logged, and the original application value or throwable is forwarded from `finally`. The installed-agent `deeplyNestedSuccessCompletesApplicationFuture` regression decodes a 10,000-level reply, verifies the returned `OK`, and asserts one successful span and duration point without `error.type`.

threads.body: [Javaagent] In supported Vert.x 5.1.0, `MultiType.getKeys()` builds a string-keyed map from the raw response pairs (see [the implementation](https://github.com/vert-x3/vertx-redis-client/blob/5.1.0/src/main/java/io/vertx/redis/client/impl/types/MultiType.java)). Distinct binary keys such as bytes `FF` and `FE` both decode to `�`, so the second value overwrites the first in that map. If the first value is a `WRONGTYPE detail` error and the second is `OK`, this traversal misses the error: the span remains successful and both the span and duration metric omit `error.type`. Iterate the single-entry wrappers and extract each value separately, so keys from different entries cannot collide. Add a regression with colliding binary keys.

@copilot Fix the native-map traversal defect identified during the response-traversal simplification, while preserving the completed removal of the getRedisErrorType testing wrapper.

Review 5622792707, comment https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20791#discussion_r4355151178, identifies a confirmed supported failure in VertxRedisClientError.children(Response). Vert.x 5.1.0 MultiType stores original Response pairs, but whole-map getKeys() and get(String) build a string-keyed map from those pairs. Binary bulk keys containing byte FF and byte FE both decode to the same replacement string; if their respective values are a WRONGTYPE error and OK, the second replaces the first before our traversal sees it. The application succeeds as intended, but instrumentation incorrectly reports success and omits error.type.

The premise is verified against https://github.com/vert-x3/vertx-redis-client/blob/5.1.0/src/main/java/io/vertx/redis/client/impl/types/MultiType.java. Its native-map iterator preserves each raw pair by returning a single-entry native MultiType wrapper. Enumerate those entries in their existing order and extract each entry's value without building a string-keyed view of the whole parent map and without recursively descending through self-wrapping native map iterators. A per-entry lookup can avoid cross-entry key collisions; use the simplest compatible approach after inspecting the actual supported implementations. Keep the iterator-stack traversal, optional cached isMap reflection for older interfaces, null-value handling, first-error order, and deep-nesting safety. Do not add a reflection framework, raw private-field access, response copies, or recursive traversal.

Cover send and batch through shared parameterization where practical, preserving existing terminal-exception precedence and completion-count assertions. Ensure this regression actually executes against a binary-preserving supported implementation such as 5.1.0; a skipped old-version test is not evidence. Use existing test conventions and only the minimal necessary test wiring. Vert.x 4.4.5 already stringifies/collapses keys during decoding, so do not require instrumentation to reconstruct an error object that the library has discarded. The existing ReplyServer writes UTF-8 Strings, so represent the required raw FF/FE bytes correctly rather than accidentally sending their UTF-8 encodings.
